name: Malta

findings.summary: Melita agreed with Ericsson to deploy the Ericsson Radio System and to modernise and expand its virtual Evolved Packet Core, preparing its Maltese mobile network for 5G.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) supplies RAN and core, so pole third. Both opened reports likely trace to the same vendor announcement; treated as corroborated on the LUX-002 precedent, reviewer may disagree. Previous vendor and value not stated. A 2018 Ericsson 'strategic 5G partner' release was seen in search only. Mobile Europe page undated.

findings.summary: Epic, the former Vodafone Malta, selected Ericsson as its exclusive 5G radio access network provider to fully modernise its existing network, including spectrum sharing, antennas and Massive MIMO.
findings.analyst_inference: RAN only; core vendor not stated. Previous RAN vendor not named, so no reversal coded. A 2025 Ericsson item (search title only) suggests the network is live on Ericsson 5G, but not opened, so tier kept at 3. Value and duration undisclosed.

findings.summary: GO Malta chose Nokia as sole strategic partner for a seven-year nationwide 5G radio access deal using AirScale equipment, extending a relationship dating from its 2007 3G launch; GO planned EUR 16m of 5G investment.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland), so pole third. RAN only; core vendor not stated. Nokia is the incumbent, not a replacement. EUR 16m is GO's planned 5G investment, not the contract value, and is not converted. Operator's majority owner is Tunisian (Tunisie Telecom), which does not change the equipment pole.

findings.local_actor: Safe City Malta Ltd (state-owned; tourism ministry)
findings.reversal_of: Huawei technology-partner agreement (MoU) for the Safe City Malta surveillance project, including lab trials
findings.summary: The government said its expired agreement with Huawei, technology partner for the Safe City Malta video-surveillance scheme, would not be renewed and began dissolving the state company; no public-space deployment was reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: per 2019 reporting the Huawei MoU covered lab-condition Safe City work and 5G testing, never a public-space contract. Reason coded commercial on the only stated reason (agreement expiry); privacy objections and a 2019 US warning preceded it, so a reviewer may judge regulatory or geopolitical. No S1/S2 source opened, so not corroborated. The Shift dates the dissolution announcement to 2024, MaltaToday to January 2023; the earlier date is used. EUR 400,000 annual budget not coded as a value.

findings.local_actor: Malta Digital Innovation Authority; Ministry for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects
findings.summary: Under the government's AI for All programme, residents aged 14+ who complete a two-hour MDIA and University of Malta AI literacy course receive a free year of ChatGPT Plus or Microsoft 365 Copilot, via e-ID.

sources.publisher: Department of Information, Government of Malta

findings.analyst_inference: Models used only through US providers' services, so pole us. Tier 3 judged from a launched, government-run national distribution with named counterparties; the release does not say whether a contract or MoU was signed, so reviewer may prefer tier 2. TechRadar places it under OpenAI for Countries. Value undisclosed.

findings.controller: Malta Digital Innovation Authority (antenna); compute host not stated
findings.financier: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (EU share of ~EUR 55m antenna programme, matched nationally)
findings.summary: EuroHPC selected Malta to host CALYPSO, an EUR 10m AI Factory Antenna led by MDIA and linked to Greece's PHAROS AI Factory, giving local users access to EuroHPC AI supercomputing; not yet operational.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: an antenna provides access to compute hosted elsewhere, and neither source names the machine or its controller (likely EU/Greek, i.e. third). Tier 2: selection with a collaboration MoU expected by mid-2026; no hardware named. No S1/S2 opened, so not corroborated. EUR 10m not converted.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase surfaced in facilities or models searches

research_gaps: Core-network vendors for Epic and GO are not established; were any Huawei or ZTE elements in Maltese mobile or fixed networks before the 2020-22 5G awards?
What did the Huawei-Malta MoU (5G testing, Safe City, joint innovation centre) commit, when was it signed, and was any Huawei equipment left in state use after Safe City Malta's dissolution?
Which supercomputer and controller serve the CALYPSO AI Factory Antenna, and was the antenna-factory MoU signed in 2026?
Is the AI for All programme a signed contract with OpenAI and Microsoft, and what does it cost the state?
Data-centre build-out since 2023 (BMIT, other operators, any hyperscaler) not found; BMIT's Zejtun facility dates from 2019 and is not AI-specific.
Submarine cable vendors for Malta's links (e.g. to Sicily) not checked for HMN Tech involvement.
